#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# worktree-guard.sh — keep `git worktree add` inside the managed lifecycle.
#
# WHY. worktree-manager.py caps concurrency at MAX_WORKTREES=5, but it counted
# only worktrees in its own registry. A raw `git worktree add` never registers,
# so the cap could not see it. Measured in a real repo: 36 worktrees under a
# cap of 5, 25 of them in `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/` paths belonging to
# sessions that had already ended. A worktree outside the repo root outlives
# its session's directory, so `git worktree prune` never reclaims it.
#
# POLICY (deliberately two-tier):
#   * a target path that ESCAPES the repo root -> DENY, always. There is no
#     legitimate use, and it is the only case that strands metadata forever.
#   * anything else -> ADVISE (exit 0 + stderr note) by default, so a
#     downstream repo with its own workflow is never broken by a surprise
#     block. Opt into hard blocking with CK_WORKTREE_GUARD=block.
#
# Registered as a BLOCKING row with matcher "Bash" and NO command_matcher:
# the registry invariant permits a command_matcher only on an advisory row,
# and an advisory row is clamped to ADVISE, which could never refuse the
# escaping-path case. The row is cheap because this script self-filters on the
# command text before doing any work.
#
# PARSING (both were live bypasses caught by test, not theory):
#   * `git -C <dir> worktree add ...` -- a flag WITH an argument before the
#     subcommand; an anchored `git\s+worktree` regex never matched it.
#   * `git worktree add -b <branch> <path>` -- `-b` consumes the next token,
#     so "first non-flag token" returned the BRANCH and the escaping <path>
#     went unexamined. Value-taking flags are skipped with their argument.
#
# ECC_HOOK_PROFILE: minimal -> off. standard/strict -> as above.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_NAME="worktree-guard"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh" ] && . "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

ROOT="$(resolve_root)"
# lib.sh appends the extractor's stderr to $LOG_FILE. If that path is not
# writable -- a repo with no .claude/hooks/ directory -- the redirection fails,
# which fails the command substitution, which made `CMD=... || exit 0` exit 0
# and the guard silently allowed EVERY `git worktree add`. It failed open in
# precisely the repos it exists to protect. Point at /dev/null unless the
# directory really exists. Found by test, not by reading.
if [ -d "$ROOT/.claude/hooks" ]; then
    LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-$ROOT/.claude/hooks/hooks.log}"
else
    LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-/dev/null}"
fi

PROFILE="${ECC_HOOK_PROFILE:-standard}"
[ "$PROFILE" = "minimal" ] && exit 0

PAYLOAD="$(cat)"

# An unreadable payload is NOT fail-closed here: this guard is a hygiene
# speed bump, not a security control, and command-guard.sh already fails
# closed on the same payload. Blocking twice on one malformed input would
# deny every Bash call for a non-security reason.
CMD="$(extract_json_field "$PAYLOAD" command)" || exit 0
[ -n "$CMD" ] || exit 0

# Self-filter: only `git worktree add` is in contract.
printf '%s' "$CMD" | grep -Eq '(^|[[:space:]])git([[:space:]]|.)*[[:space:]]worktree[[:space:]]+add([[:space:]]|$)' || exit 0

# First non-flag token after `add` is the target path.
TARGET="$(printf '%s' "$CMD" | awk '
    { for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "add" && $(i-1) == "worktree") { s = i + 1; break } }
    s { for (i = s; i <= NF; i++) {
            t = $i
            if (t == "-b" || t == "-B" || t == "--reason") { i++; continue }
            if (substr(t, 1, 1) == "-") continue
            print t; exit } }
')"
TARGET="${TARGET%\"}"; TARGET="${TARGET#\"}"
TARGET="${TARGET%\'}"; TARGET="${TARGET#\'}"

# A target the guard cannot evaluate is a target it cannot clear. Review found
# four ordinary spellings that reached an out-of-repo path while being
# classified as a safe relative path, because this guard reads the LITERAL
# command text and the shell that runs it does not:
#   git worktree add $(echo /tmp/evil)   -> token "$(echo"
#   git worktree add ~/evil              -> token "~/evil"
#   P=/tmp/evil; git worktree add "$P"   -> token "$P"
#   git -C /other/tree worktree add rel  -> "rel" resolves under /other/tree
# The first three are refused because they are UNRESOLVABLE, not because they
# are known-bad. The fourth is refused because -C moves the frame of reference
# this guard measures against, and it cannot follow.
unresolvable() {
    # A target carrying a control character (newline, tab) cannot be reasoned
    # about as ONE path; refuse rather than guess which line the shell acts on.
    # NOT written as a case pattern: `$(printf '\n')` strips its own trailing
    # newline and expands to the EMPTY string, making the pattern *""* -- which
    # matches every target and denied every worktree add. Caught by test.
    printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C grep -q '[[:cntrl:]]' && return 0
    case "$1" in
        *'$'*|*'`'*|'~'*|*'*'*|*'?'*) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

redirected() {
    # -C / --git-dir / --work-tree appearing BEFORE the worktree subcommand.
    printf '%s' "$CMD" | awk '
        { for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
              if ($i == "worktree") exit found
              if ($i == "-C" || $i == "--git-dir" || $i == "--work-tree") found = 1
              if (index($i, "--git-dir=") == 1) found = 1
              if (index($i, "--work-tree=") == 1) found = 1
          } }
        END { exit found }
    ' && return 1 || return 0
}

escapes_root() {
    case "$1" in
        "") return 1 ;;
        /*) case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) return 1 ;; *) return 0 ;; esac ;;
        *..*) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
    hlog "DENY" "git worktree add with no parseable target"
    printf 'worktree-guard: refusing `git worktree add` — no target path could be parsed.\n' >&2
    printf '  Use: python3 .claude/operations/scripts/worktree-manager.py create <slug>\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

if unresolvable "$TARGET"; then
    hlog "DENY" "unresolvable git worktree add target: $TARGET"
    printf 'worktree-guard: refusing `git worktree add %s` — the target contains shell\n' "$TARGET" >&2
    printf '  expansion this guard cannot evaluate, so it cannot be shown to stay inside\n' >&2
    printf '  the repo. Pass a literal path, or use:\n' >&2
    printf '    python3 .claude/operations/scripts/worktree-manager.py create <slug>\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

if redirected; then
    hlog "DENY" "git worktree add under -C/--git-dir redirection: $TARGET"
    printf 'worktree-guard: refusing `git worktree add` combined with -C/--git-dir/--work-tree.\n' >&2
    printf '  The redirect moves the root a relative target resolves against, and this guard\n' >&2
    printf '  measures against the current repo. Run it from the target repo instead.\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

if escapes_root "$TARGET"; then
    hlog "DENY" "git worktree add outside repo root: $TARGET"
    printf 'worktree-guard: refusing `git worktree add` at %s — the path escapes the repo root.\n' "$TARGET" >&2
    printf '  A worktree outside the repo outlives the directory that held it; `git worktree prune`\n' >&2
    printf '  cannot reclaim it and the registry never sees it. Create it under .worktrees/ instead:\n' >&2
    printf '    python3 .claude/operations/scripts/worktree-manager.py create <slug>\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

if [ "${CK_WORKTREE_GUARD:-advise}" = "block" ]; then
    hlog "DENY" "raw git worktree add (CK_WORKTREE_GUARD=block): $TARGET"
    printf 'worktree-guard: refusing raw `git worktree add` (CK_WORKTREE_GUARD=block).\n' >&2
    printf '  Use: python3 .claude/operations/scripts/worktree-manager.py create <slug>\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

hlog "ADVISE" "raw git worktree add bypasses the cap: $TARGET"
printf 'worktree-guard: this `git worktree add` bypasses the MAX_WORKTREES cap and is not registered.\n' >&2
printf '  Prefer: python3 .claude/operations/scripts/worktree-manager.py create <slug>\n' >&2
printf '  Set CK_WORKTREE_GUARD=block to make this a hard refusal.\n' >&2
exit 0
operations.description: A3: advisory guard on raw `git worktree add`; hard refusal only for a path escaping the repo root
A4: register worktree-guard (blocking tier, self-filtering — a command_matcher row may only be advisory)

"""Behavioural coverage for worktree-guard.sh (plan-repo-hygiene-gates, phase A).

Every command below is a spelling that DEFEATED an earlier draft of this guard.
Seven distinct defects were found here across two adversarial reviews and two
rounds of execution testing; each case is the regression test for one of them.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
GUARD = ROOT / ".claude" / "hooks" / "worktree-guard.sh"

DENY, ALLOW = 2, 0


def _git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo)] + list(args),
                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)


def run_guard(command, cwd=None, env_extra=None):
    """Drive the real hook.

    The guard resolves its root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the
    PROCESS CWD (lib.sh:resolve_root) and ignores CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR entirely.
    An earlier version of this helper set that env var and believed it was
    redirecting the guard's root; it was not, and the prefix-collision test
    below passed for the wrong reason. Round-2 review caught it. Drive the root
    with cwd, which is what the script actually reads.
    """
    payload = json.dumps({"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": command}})
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["ECC_HOOK_PROFILE"] = "standard"   # forced explicitly, never inherited
    env.update(env_extra or {})
    return subprocess.run(["bash", str(GUARD)], input=payload, text=True,
                          capture_output=True, env=env, cwd=str(cwd or ROOT),
                          timeout=30).returncode


# --- the escaping-path guarantee -------------------------------------------
# The first four were live bypasses: the guard reads the LITERAL command text,
# and the shell that executes it expands what the guard could not.
@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", [
    "git worktree add $(echo /tmp/evil)",
    "git worktree add `echo /tmp/evil`",
    "git worktree add ~/evil",
    'git worktree add "$P"',
    "git -C /other/tree worktree add rel",
    "git --git-dir=/other/.git worktree add rel",
    "git --work-tree=/other worktree add rel",
    "git worktree add /private/tmp/x/wt",
    "git worktree add ../escape",
    "git worktree add /tmp/a/../../etc",
    "git worktree add -b br /tmp/escaping",     # -b consumes a token; path must still be read
])
def test_escaping_or_unresolvable_target_is_refused(command):
    assert run_guard(command) == DENY, f"guard allowed {command!r}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", [
    "git worktree add .worktrees/foo",
    "git worktree add -b br .worktrees/ok",
    "git worktree add --detach .worktrees/d",
    "git status",
    "git worktree list",
    "git worktree remove .worktrees/foo",
    'echo "git worktree add /tmp/x"',           # merely mentioning it is not doing it
])
def test_legitimate_commands_are_not_blocked(command):
    assert run_guard(command) == ALLOW, f"guard blocked {command!r}"


def test_prefix_confusion_is_not_a_bypass(tmp_path):
    """/repo-evil must not be treated as inside /repo.

    A REAL repo, entered by cwd -- the guard's root comes from git, so a
    directory that was never `git init`-ed would silently resolve to whatever
    repo pytest happens to be running in, and the assertion would prove nothing.
    """
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    root.mkdir()
    _git(root, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    sibling = tmp_path / "repo-evil"
    sibling.mkdir()
    assert run_guard(f"git worktree add {sibling}/wt", cwd=root) == DENY


def test_in_repo_path_is_allowed_from_a_scratch_root(tmp_path):
    """Positive control for the test above: same scratch root, inside path.

    Without this, a guard that denied EVERYTHING would still pass the
    prefix-collision test.
    """
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    root.mkdir()
    _git(root, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    assert run_guard("git worktree add .worktrees/ok", cwd=root) == ALLOW


def test_minimal_profile_disables_the_guard():
    assert run_guard("git worktree add /tmp/evil",
                     env_extra={"ECC_HOOK_PROFILE": "minimal"}) == ALLOW


def test_block_mode_refuses_even_an_in_repo_path():
    assert run_guard("git worktree add .worktrees/ok",
                     env_extra={"CK_WORKTREE_GUARD": "block"}) == DENY
operations.description: A4: one regression test per guard defect found in review and execution testing
